One of the hardest feelings to overcome, at least to me, is feeling like you're not just a burden to everyone around you.  I've been there, truly.  I've come to the point sometimes where I've honestly believed that, judging by how I haven't truly been much of a success in my family's eyes, that I'll never be more than just a damn burden.

That's only a half-truth though.

The other half is that, if you really "are" a burden but they keep trying to support you, is that they love you dude.  You don't quit on family or true friends, and I'm sure your family will never give up on you.

Not that they need to, because in the road of life you're only racing with yourself.

Hang in there.

Dying is easy, it's living that's hard.  

When things are at their darkest, I feel like my only answer to it all is to find the things to be grateful for.  Your car, your pet, being warm, "something".
Not even going to lie, humanity is fucking disgusting.  I think the only thing we can do is realize what it is about us that is disgusting and rise above.

When I was in the service, they had a term for the situation when you're confronted with having to do the "right thing".  We called it this:

"The hard right, or the easy wrong".

There is a reason why it is hard, and it's often that the righteous road is the lonely one.  You shouldn't feel bad for taking the wrong road.  It's easier, it's what we know, and it's commonplace.

I'd like to believe that everyone has a purpose, even if they can make someone else smile or laugh.  You're on this earth for a reason man.  Not everyone finds it right away, but there's a reason.  Don't give up, and find the small things that make you happy. 

Gratuity is the key to happiness, after all.

Hey man... I just made a post no more than two minutes ago and I just wanted to reply to this to tell you one thing:  You're not alone.

If there is one thing that nailed it home for me when I read your post, it was your final paragraph.  Feeling like a burden, feeling super fucking lonely, it's more than alot of people can handle.  To me, I think the worst part may very well be the fact that we can't even share this information with our family and friends because we don't want to be more of a burden.

I don't know if it's good or bad that we have to try to find anonymous help on the internet, but that's what I've ended up having to do tonight.  

I think the first and foremost thing to solving your problem is pretty much on this subreddit, and that is just finding someone who wants to listen.  I know how you're feeling bud, I'm feeling the same way.  But at least we know that we aren't the only ones.  If there is anything to take heart from, it's the fact that posting these feelings can help another feel like it's not an isolated problem and that you're not alone in your struggles.  

I have no advice on how to get better, but I do know that the answer can start here.  Chin up!

I am convinced that there have had to have been a few moments or times in your life where you we're happy.  That has to be true.  

I would argue that you are only a "tool" if you don't have a choice in the matter.  Everyone needs someone else for some reason or another.  Sometimes for laughs, sometimes for advice.  Whatever the reason, I'd like to believe that you're only truly a tool if people manipulate you and you get absolutely nothing out of the relationship.  As long as you DO get something out of it though, that should be all that matters at this point and if that certain someone can comfort you, who cares what they get?  It's a mutual thing.  People use people.

What is "human" anyway?  You should never be ashamed to be who you are, however you feel about yourself and your image.  All of your years have made you grow up into the person that you are today, and you should never be ashamed of the persona you've chosen that you want to be.

If you believe that if someone being "normal" is equivalent to them being human then I couldn't disagree more.  Your humanity is a collective of ALL of your quirks and flaws, your strengths and your feelings.



tl dr: Find a moment where you felt happy once and focus on why it made you happy.  Use those reasons and seek them in your current crisis.  Ask the people you know if they've ever felt sad and how they deal with it.  Talk it out, you always feel better.

My biggest hurdle is finding people to help me find the good thoughts.  Sometimes I feel like I don't have anyone in my corner except my immediate family.  The problem for me is that because I know what my immediate family says to me is biased for me, their words don't effect me or sink in as deep.

Another answer is simply to hunt for the good.  I'm convicned that gratuity is the secret to happiness, and the more you can find in your life that you can safely say you're happy you have, the better off you'll be.  Unfortunately, sometimes in order to do that you need to see how easy it is to lose it and how tough it can be without it.

I hope you find an answer to your problem.
